subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Development of the model of the atom

questions.q: In which state of matter are the particles arranged in a regular pattern and only able to vibrate about fixed positions?
options: Solid
Liquid
Gas
Plasma
questions.explain: In a solid the particles are closely packed in a regular arrangement and can only vibrate about fixed positions.

questions.q: What is the name of the change of state from a gas to a liquid?
options: Condensing
Evaporating
Melting
Subliming
questions.explain: Condensing is the change of state from gas to liquid as particles lose energy.

questions.q: Why can a gas be compressed much more easily than a solid?
options: Its particles are far apart with large spaces between them
Its particles are heavier than those in a solid
Its particles are held in fixed positions
Its particles are larger than solid particles
questions.explain: Gas particles are widely spaced, so they can be pushed closer together, whereas solid particles are already touching.

questions.q: Which statement is a limitation of the simple particle model?
options: It assumes there are no forces of attraction between particles
It assumes particles are always moving
It assumes solids have a fixed shape
It assumes gases fill their container
questions.explain: The simple model treats particles as solid inelastic spheres with no forces between them, which is not fully accurate.

questions.q: A substance has strong forces of attraction between its particles. What does this suggest about its melting point?
options: It will have a relatively high melting point
It will have a very low melting point
It cannot melt at all
Its melting point is unaffected by the forces
questions.explain: More energy is needed to overcome stronger forces of attraction, giving a higher melting point.

questions.q: A substance has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container and its particles are close together yet free to move. Which state is it in?
options: Liquid
Solid
Gas
It is not in any state
questions.explain: A liquid has a fixed volume, flows to take the shape of its container, and its particles are close but able to move past one another.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: A proton carries a relative charge of +1, equal and opposite to the electron's -1.

questions.q: What is the relative mass of an electron compared with a proton?
options: Very small (about 1/1835)
questions.explain: An electron has a negligible relative mass, roughly 1/1835 that of a proton.

questions.q: Which sub-atomic particle has no electric charge?
options: Neutron
Proton
Electron
Ion
questions.explain: The neutron is neutral, carrying a relative charge of 0.

questions.q: What does the atomic number of an element tell you?
options: The number of protons in the nucleus
The total number of protons and neutrons
The number of neutrons in the nucleus
The number of occupied electron shells
questions.explain: The atomic (proton) number equals the number of protons, which defines the element.

questions.q: Why does an atom have no overall electric charge?
options: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons
It has equal numbers of protons and neutrons
It has no charged particles
The neutrons cancel out the electrons
questions.explain: The equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons balance to give a neutral atom.

questions.q: Almost all of the mass of an atom is found in which region?
options: The nucleus
The electron shells
The space around the nucleus
Spread evenly throughout the atom
questions.explain: The mass of an atom is concentrated in the nucleus, which contains the protons and neutrons.

questions.q: An atom of sodium has a mass number of 23 and an atomic number of 11. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explain: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 23 - 11 = 12.

questions.q: What is the electron configuration of a sodium atom (atomic number 11)?
questions.explain: Filling shells (2, then 8, then 1) for 11 electrons gives the configuration 2,8,1.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes isotopes of the same element?
options: Same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
Same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons
Different numbers of protons and electrons
Same mass number but different atomic numbers
questions.explain: Isotopes have the same atomic number (protons) but different mass numbers because they have different numbers of neutrons.

questions.q: Why do different isotopes of an element have identical chemical properties?
options: They have the same number and arrangement of electrons
They have the same number of neutrons
They have the same mass number
They have different numbers of protons
questions.explain: Chemical properties depend on electrons, and isotopes have the same electronic structure.

questions.q: Chlorine is 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
Which scientist discovered the electron, leading to the plum pudding model of the atom?
options: J. J. Thomson
John Dalton
Ernest Rutherford
Niels Bohr
questions.explain: Thomson's discovery of the electron led to the plum pudding model of a positive sphere with embedded electrons.

questions.q: In the alpha particle scattering experiment, most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil. What did this suggest about the atom?
options: The atom is mostly empty space
The atom is a solid sphere
The atom has no nucleus
Mass is spread evenly through the atom
questions.explain: Most particles passing straight through showed the atom is largely empty space, with mass concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

questions.q: What key idea did Niels Bohr add to the model of the atom?
options: Electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy levels (shells)
The atom contains a small positive nucleus
Atoms are tiny indivisible spheres
The neutron exists in the nucleus
questions.explain: Bohr proposed that electrons occupy fixed shells or energy levels at set distances from the nucleus.
